cases.label: cm copy / 방금 뭘 하려고 했어
cases.why: the case recorded on 2026-09-10, verbatim. Everything else here is it, enlarged.

cases.label: cm font / 아까 뭐 눌렀어
cases.why: the offer is a combo box rather than a button, so the offered line names a role the model never typed.

cases.label: cm help / 뭐 하려던 거야
cases.why: a link, and the shortest of the five phrasings.

cases.label: cm close / 방금 뭐 하려고 했지
cases.why: the one offer whose repetition would cost something real. If the tense matters anywhere it should matter here.

cases.label: cm select / 너 방금 뭐 했어
cases.why: phrased as what it DID rather than what it meant to do — the question the false past tense answered truthfully.

cases.label: paint eraser / 방금 뭘 하려고 했어
cases.why: the same wording as case one on the 123-widget screen: is the effect the wording or the size of the list?

cases.label: paint red / 아까 뭐 눌렀어
cases.why: a list item among twenty near-identical ones.

cases.label: paint pencil / 뭐 하려던 거야
cases.why: a tool, and the ask names the role in Korean where the widget names it in English.

cases.label: paint undo / 방금 뭐 하려고 했지
cases.why: undo is itself about the past, so both turns point backwards.

cases.label: paint crop / 너 방금 뭐 했어
cases.why: the fifth phrasing on the second screen.

cases.label: cm copy / EN what were you about to do
cases.then: What were you about to do?
cases.why: English in and out. The new line is English prose; a result that only held in Korean would be a different finding and these two cases are the only ones that can show it.

cases.label: paint eraser / EN what did you just try
cases.then: What did you just try to do?
cases.why: the second English case, on the other screen.

cases.label: si find / 방금 뭘 하려고 했어
cases.why: case one's wording on the longest prompt captured — 152 widget lines between the offer and the question.

cases.label: si hardware / 아까 뭐 눌렀어
cases.why: a tree item — a role neither of the first two screens offers, so the offered line names a kind of thing the set had never carried.

cases.label: si minimize / 뭐 하려던 거야
cases.why: an offer whose repetition costs something visible, on the long screen.

cases.label: si edit menu / 방금 뭐 하려고 했지
cases.why: a menu item on a screen that also lists a menu bar and a menu item both called 'System' — the name is not the key here either.

cases.label: si summary / 너 방금 뭐 했어
cases.why: 'System Summary' is three widgets — a tree item, a list and a header — so the offered line names one of three things wearing one name.

cases.label: si find / EN what were you about to do
cases.then: What were you about to do?
cases.why: the English pair of case one, on the longest prompt.

cases.label: crd close / 방금 뭘 하려고 했어
cases.why: case one's wording on the shortest prompt captured — 12 widget lines. With the 152 of system-information it brackets the two screens the old set had.

cases.label: crd extensions / 아까 뭐 눌렀어
cases.why: **the widget's own name is Korean**, so the offered line quotes Korean inside English prose. No other screen here can produce that, and `narrated` can finally be true of a Korean reply.

cases.label: crd minimize / 뭐 하려던 거야
cases.why: the shortest phrasing on the shortest screen — the least of everything, and the case most likely to work if anything does.

cases.label: crd password / 방금 뭐 하려고 했지
cases.why: saving a password is the one offer here a person would mind being repeated.

cases.label: crd settings / 너 방금 뭐 했어
cases.why: the longest widget name in the fixtures — 'Chrome Remote Desktop 맞춤설정 및 제어', mixed script, quoted whole into the offered line.

cases.label: crd extensions / EN what did you just try
cases.then: What did you just try to do?
cases.why: English in, and the name it has to hand back is Korean.

cases.label: cm copy / 응 그렇게 해줘
cases.why: 'they have not accepted' is now in the prompt and they have just accepted. A model that reads that line as 'do not touch this' fails here — this is the control the treatment itself threatens. ACTED at f842432 in both tense arms.

cases.label: paint eraser / 어 눌러줘
cases.why: the same, on the larger screen. IGNORED 3 of 3 in both arms — one of the two failures this enlargement exists to make scoreable.

cases.label: cm font / 네 해주세요
cases.why: the formal register, in case acceptance is only recognised casually. ACTED.

cases.label: paint red / 그래 진행해
cases.why: 'go ahead' rather than 'yes'. IGNORED as the worst of 3 (acted once) — the second failure, and the one case in the group that disagreed with itself.

cases.label: cm copy / 응
cases.why: the shortest acceptance in the language, on the case that already works with a phrase. If this fails and the phrase passes, the fix is about parsing, not memory.

cases.label: paint eraser / 어
cases.why: the same pairing on the case that already fails with a phrase.

cases.label: cm help / ㅇㅇ
cases.why: typed rather than spoken — two consonants, no vowel. A tokeniser's worst case and what people actually type.

cases.label: paint pencil / 그래
cases.why: 'sure', which is also an ordinary conversational filler — the acceptance most easily read as small talk.

cases.label: cm copy / EN yes
cases.why: English in and out. The offered line is English prose; a defect that only exists in Korean is a different finding and these four English cases are what can show it.

cases.label: paint eraser / EN go ahead
cases.why: the second English bare case, on the other screen.

cases.label: cm close / 응 그거 해줘
cases.why: the one acceptance whose repetition costs something real. If a fix makes the agent act on anything after an offer, this is where it hurts.

cases.label: paint crop / 네 그렇게 해주세요
cases.why: formal register on the larger screen; the pair of case 3.

cases.label: cm select / 좋아 그렇게 하자
cases.why: 'let's do that' — first person plural, no imperative at all.

cases.label: paint undo / 어 그거로 해줘
cases.why: 'that one' — a pronoun pointing at the offer rather than a name.

cases.label: cm close / EN yes, please do that
cases.why: the English phrase against the English bare 'yes' on case 9.

cases.label: paint crop / EN okay, do it
cases.why: the fourth English case, on the other screen.

cases.label: cm advanced / 응 그렇게 부탁해
cases.why: a check box, the one role on this screen no acceptance case had; and the wording is the one shared by all four screens.

cases.label: cm minimize / 네
cases.why: the bare polite yes — one syllable, and the register the phrased '네 해주세요' already passes in. If '네' fails where '네 해주세요' passes, length is the variable.

cases.label: paint magnifier / 응 그렇게 부탁해
cases.why: the same wording as the Character Map case above, 102 widget lines further down the prompt.

cases.label: paint save / 네
cases.why: the bare '네' on the long screen, and Save is an app bar button — a role the group carried nowhere else.

cases.label: si find / 응 그렇게 해줘
cases.why: the wording that passes on Character Map, on the longest prompt. If it fails here and passes there, distance is doing the work.

cases.label: si hardware / 어 눌러줘
cases.why: the wording that fails on Paint 3 of 3 — the case that literally asked 'which button?'. On a third screen it is no longer one screen's.

cases.label: si minimize / 네 해주세요
cases.why: the formal register at 152 lines.

cases.label: si edit menu / 그래 진행해
cases.why: 'go ahead' rather than 'yes', on a menu item.

cases.label: si summary / 응 그렇게 부탁해
cases.why: the offer names one of three widgets called 'System Summary', so accepting it has to re-pick the same role as well as the same name.

cases.label: si find / EN okay, do it
cases.why: English phrase, longest prompt. Pairs with the Paint case of the same words so the English row is two wordings on four screens, not four.

cases.label: si find / 응
cases.why: the shortest acceptance in the language on the longest prompt — the far corner of both axes at once, and the cell most likely to fail.

cases.label: si components / 그래
cases.why: 'sure', which is also ordinary small talk, at 152 lines' distance from the offer.

cases.label: si software env / ㅇㅇ
cases.why: two consonants and no vowel — the typed yes. On Character Map it came back with SYSTEM's own fallback sentence.

cases.label: si minimize / EN yes
cases.why: the bare English yes on the long screen.

cases.label: crd close / 응 그렇게 해줘
cases.why: the Character Map wording on the shortest prompt there is. If acceptance is a distance effect this is the cell that should pass first.

cases.label: crd extensions / 어 눌러줘
cases.why: the Paint wording at 12 lines instead of 123, and the offered name is Korean. Failing here would say the wording, not the distance.

cases.label: crd minimize / 네 해주세요
cases.why: the formal register on the short screen.

cases.label: crd password / 그래 진행해
cases.why: the acceptance on this screen that would cost something if it were dropped and the person had to say it twice.

cases.label: crd settings / 응 그렇게 부탁해
cases.why: the four-screen wording again, on the longest widget name in the fixtures.

cases.label: crd close / EN yes, please do that
cases.why: English in, a Korean widget name offered back, and an English acceptance of it.

cases.label: crd close / 응
cases.why: the near corner against `si find / 응`'s far one: same two turns, same two words, 140 widget lines of difference.

cases.label: crd restore / 그래
cases.why: 'sure' on the short screen; the ask names the action where the widget names the state ('복구').

cases.label: crd extensions / ㅇㅇ
cases.why: the typed yes on the short screen.

cases.label: crd extensions / EN go ahead
cases.why: the fourth English bare case; the pair of Paint's, on the other end of the axis.

cases.label: cm copy far / 응 해줘
cases.why: the case that accepts correctly at distance 1: if it fails here, distance is the variable and nothing about the wording is.

cases.label: paint eraser far / 응 해줘
cases.why: the case that fails at distance 1. Failing here as well is the null result.

cases.label: cm font far / 그래 해줘
cases.why: a combo box rather than a button, four turns back.

cases.label: paint red far / EN yes go ahead
cases.why: English acceptance of a Korean ask, at distance. Two things at once, deliberately: this one is a probe, not a control.

cases.label: cm close far / EN yes go ahead
cases.why: the mixed case Character Map lacked, so all four screens now carry one.

cases.label: paint crop far / 그래 해줘
cases.why: the second Korean far case on Paint, on an offer that accepts correctly at distance 1.

cases.label: si find far / 응 해줘
cases.why: distance 5 on the longest prompt — conversational distance and prompt distance at their maxima together.

cases.label: si minimize far / 그래 해줘
cases.why: the second Korean far case on the long screen.

cases.label: si hardware far / EN yes go ahead
cases.why: English acceptance of a Korean ask, five turns back, on a tree item.

cases.label: crd close far / 응 해줘
cases.why: distance 5 on the shortest prompt: if the offer is still reachable anywhere, here.

cases.label: crd extensions far / 그래 해줘
cases.why: the second Korean far case on the short screen.

cases.label: crd password far / EN yes go ahead
cases.why: the mixed far case on the fourth screen; the offered name is Korean and the acceptance is not.

cases.label: cm / 글자 복사하고 싶어 -> 복사 눌러줘
cases.why: a vague want, then the target by name. The ask is deliberately not the restatement.

cases.label: paint / 지우고 싶어 -> 지우개 눌러줘
cases.why: the same shape on the 123-widget screen.

cases.label: cm / 이 창 닫고 싶어 -> 닫기 눌러줘

cases.label: paint / 자르고 싶어 -> 자르기 눌러줘
cases.why: the fourth, and the Korean name is a verb where the widget's is a noun.

cases.label: si / 하드웨어 쪽 보고 싶어 -> 하드웨어 리소스 눌러줘
cases.why: the first named target on a tree item, and on the longest prompt.

cases.label: si / 시스템 정보 보고 싶어 -> 시스템 요약 눌러줘
cases.why: **three widgets are called 'System Summary'** — tree item, list, header. The pair is the key and the label is not, which is the Font : defect on a third screen.

cases.label: crd / 이 창 닫고 싶어 -> 닫기 눌러줘
cases.why: the Character Map case word for word, on a screen whose Close button is named in Korean — so the restatement and the widget name are the same string.

cases.label: crd / 확장 프로그램 보고 싶어 -> 확장 프로그램 눌러줘
cases.why: the fourth screen's second named target.

cases.label: cm copy / 아니 됐어
cases.why: the plainest refusal, on the case that accepts correctly. AGAIN here means it re-offered the very thing that was just turned down.

cases.label: paint eraser / 아니야 하지 마
cases.why: an explicit prohibition rather than a decline.

cases.label: cm font / 됐어 안 해도 돼
cases.why: 'it's fine, you don't have to' — polite, and the one most easily read as assent.

cases.label: paint crop / EN no, never mind
cases.why: English refusal against the English acceptances, so a language effect in one group can be read against the other.

cases.label: cm copy / EN no, don't do that
cases.why: the English refusal Character Map lacked; an explicit prohibition, so the English row carries both a decline and a prohibition.

cases.label: paint undo / 아니 지금은 하지 마
cases.why: 'not now' — a refusal with a time in it, which is the one most easily read as 'later, then'.

cases.label: si close / 아니 됐어
cases.why: the plainest refusal on the longest prompt, against the same words on Character Map.

cases.label: si edit menu / 아니야 하지 마
cases.why: an explicit prohibition at 152 lines.

cases.label: si find / EN no, never mind
cases.why: the English refusal on the long screen, the same words as Paint's.

cases.label: crd close / 아니 됐어
cases.why: the plainest refusal on the shortest prompt — the same two turns as `crd close / 응` and the opposite correct answer.

cases.label: crd password / 됐어 안 해도 돼
cases.why: 'you don't have to' — polite, and about the one offer here worth refusing.

cases.label: crd close / EN no, never mind
cases.why: the English refusal on the fourth screen; two wordings over four screens, like the English acceptances.

cases.label: cm copy -> font
cases.why: a new target while an offer is outstanding. The label/combo box pair is why the verdict is scored on the pair and not on the name.

cases.why: 'also' — the previous offer still stands and the new one is additive.

cases.label: cm help -> copy
cases.why: case one in the other order, so a stuck re-offer here is Help rather than Copy.

cases.label: paint red -> crop
cases.why: an unrelated new request: no correction, no reference to the past.

cases.label: si find -> edit menu
cases.why: 'then make it the edit menu instead' — the same shape as the case that broke, on the longest prompt.

cases.label: si minimize -> software env
cases.why: 'also' — the previous offer stands and the new one is additive, on a tree item.

cases.label: crd close -> minimize
cases.why: a new target while an offer stands, on the shortest prompt. Close and Minimize sit next to each other in the list and both are named in Korean.

cases.label: crd password -> extensions
cases.why: the additive form on the fourth screen.
